info.title: humpyard admin API
info.description: The operator surface of a humpyard gateway (ADR 0027). Opened only by an admin credential defined in the configuration's `[admin]` section; a client key never opens it. Without a configured credential the whole namespace answers 404. Every operation lists the scope it needs under `security`, and the error codes it can answer with under `x-error-codes`; a test fails when this document and the served routes differ.

post.summary: Turn edits into a validated patch against the configuration file (nothing is written)
post.description: Applies the edits, in order, to the text of the configuration file with a format-preserving editor, loads the result the way a reload does, and returns a unified diff and the fingerprint the new text would have. Key hashes, credential hashes and provider header values are shown as `<redacted>`, so the diff is for review and not for `patch(1)`. The file, the ledger and the running configuration are never changed. `fingerprint` must be the file's current fingerprint (`GET /admin/v1/config`, `config.fingerprint`). The credential also needs `read` to learn it.

200.description: The patch. `changed` is false, `diff` is empty and `fingerprint` equals `base_fingerprint` when the edits leave the text as it was.

400.description: A malformed body, more than 64 edits (`invalid_request`), or an edit that is malformed, outside the editable sections, or does not fit the file (`invalid_edit`, with `error.index`).

409.description: `fingerprint` is not the file's now (`stale_fingerprint`); `error.current_fingerprint` is.

get.description: A heavy read: it folds up to 50,000 ledger rows, so at most one heavy read runs at a time on the admin surface and another is answered 503 `admin_busy` with `Retry-After`, never queued. Identical reads (same `key`, `group_by`, `window` and filters) share one result for ten seconds; `computed_at_ms` says when it was computed.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Only the statistics of this client key; omit for every key.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: How far back, for example `6h` or `7d`; default `24h`; at most the days of decisions kept. A longer window is a 400 naming `window`.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: `route` (default), `target`, `endpoint`, `actor` or `owner`. The last two count by who the key was for (the actor it names, or the person that actor acts for); calls with none are the group `(none)`.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: Only this route.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Only this target.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Bucket width, for example `5m` or `1h`; at least `1m`, and at most 400 buckets in the window. By default the finest of 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 6h, 12h and 1d that gives at most 120 buckets.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most groups returned, busiest first, from 1 to 25; default 8. `omitted_groups` counts the rest.

schema.description: Statistics over time. Only the fields listed here are part of the contract.

computed_at_ms.description: When the answer was computed, in unix milliseconds. A repeat of the same read within ten seconds states the same time.

now_ms.description: The end of the window; the last bucket is the one containing it.

truncated.description: The window held more decisions than the row cap, so the oldest were left out.

covered_since_ms.description: When truncated, the time of the oldest decision counted: buckets before it are unread, not quiet. Null otherwise.

omitted_groups.description: Groups with requests in the window that `limit` left out.

503.description: Another heavy read is running on the admin surface (`admin_busy`), or the ledger could not be read in time. Nothing was queued; retry after the `Retry-After` seconds.

get.description: The statistics of `GET /admin/v1/stats` in equal time buckets, for the busiest groups. Buckets start at whole multiples of the interval since the Unix epoch and every bucket from the one holding the start of the window to the one holding now is present; a bucket with no requests has zero counts and null rates and percentiles. The last bucket is still filling. Counted by the same rules and from the same decision rows (at most 50,000, newest first) as `GET /admin/v1/stats`, so a group's bucket counts add up to its totals. A read is one of the heavy reads: one at a time, shared for ten seconds, shed with 503 `admin_busy`.

adminBearer.description: An admin credential's secret. The scope named in an operation's `security` is one of `read`, `overrides` or `credentials`.

scope.description: With `admin_scope_required`: the scope the credential lacks.

index.description: With `invalid_edit`: the position of the edit, counting from 0.

current_fingerprint.description: With `stale_fingerprint`: the fingerprint of the file now.

expires.description: A UTC time, or null when it does not expire.

revoked.description: True while a revocation is in force.

created_by.description: `admin:<id>` for an admin credential, otherwise a client key id.

expires_in_secs.description: Default four hours, at most the `[overrides]` maximum.

ResponseSignal.description: One fact about an answer (ADR 0030): `empty_output` (finished with no text and no tool call; reasoning alone does not count), `truncated_output` (the provider stopped it at its output limit), `bad_tool_call` (a tool call with no name, or with arguments that are neither blank nor a JSON object) or `cut_stream` (the provider's stream ended or failed before its final chunk). Only that a fact is set is kept, never any text.

ResponseSignalCounts.description: How the group's answer calls fared on the response signals: `observed` is the number of answer calls whose signals are known, and each other field counts those that carried that signal, so a rate is a count over `observed`. Calls with unknown signals (written before ledger schema v13, routing-time judge calls) are in neither figure.

Decision.description: A routing decision, as `GET /v1/decisions` returns it. Only the fields listed here are part of the contract; others may be present.

ts_ms.description: When the decision was made, in epoch milliseconds.

key.description: The client key the request came in with.

actor.description: The actor the key named when the request was made; null when it named none.

owner.description: The person the request's usage rolls up to: the actor's owner for an agent, the actor itself for a human. Null when there is none.

request.description: Facts about the request: `stream`, `prompt_tokens_estimate`, `tools`, `images`, and `repaired_tool_arguments` when some were.

response_signals.description: The signals set on the call that served the request, read from the usage ledger. Absent when none is set, when they are unknown (a decision from before schema v13) and while the answer is still streaming.

StatsGroup.description: Performance of one group over the window, as `GET /v1/stats` returns it. Only the fields listed here are part of the contract; others may be present.

failure_rate.description: Failed attempts over attempts; null when there were no attempts.

fallback_rate.description: Requests that fell back over requests; null when there were no requests.

latency_ms.description: Time to answer over the window's answer calls, in milliseconds; each is null when there were none.

avg_cost_usd.description: Average cost of an answer call in US dollars; null when there were no answer calls or no price.

avg_tokens.description: Average tokens of an answer call; null when there were no answer calls.

current_latency_ms.description: With `group_by=target`: the smoothed time to answer that `fastest` routes see now, from memory, so it can differ from the percentiles; null until the target has answered.

latency_samples.description: With `group_by=target`: how many answers the smoothed figure is built from.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the configuration file the editor last read.

ConfigEdit.description: One typed change. `path` is table names, keys and array positions inside `providers`, `targets`, `routes`, `profiles`, `aliases`, `budget`, `health`, `overrides` or `keys` (under `keys` only `set` and `remove`, never a key's `sha256`). `value` is required by `set` and `add_table` (an object for `add_table`); `remove` and `remove_table` take none. At most 8 path segments; values nest at most 4 deep.

value.description: Any JSON value except null; an object for `add_table`.

fingerprint.description: What the file's fingerprint would be with the edits applied.

diff.description: A unified diff with three lines of context, empty when nothing changed. For review: masked values do not apply with `patch(1)`.

EndpointHealth.description: The breaker state of one endpoint of a target.

cooldown_remaining_ms.description: Milliseconds until the endpoint is tried again; null when it is not cooling down.

cooldown_source.description: Why it is cooling down: its own failures or a provider's `Retry-After`; null when it is not.

Health.description: Skipped endpoints, latency, the loaded configuration and the last reload, as `GET /v1/health`.

current_latency_ms.description: The smoothed time to answer; null until the target has answered.

latency_samples.description: How many answers the figure is built from; null until the target has answered.

at_ms.description: When the last reload ran; null before the first.

SeriesBucket.description: One bucket of one group. A bucket with no requests has zero counts and null rates and percentiles, never 0.

start_ms.description: Start of the bucket, a whole multiple of `interval_ms`, in unix milliseconds.

requests.description: Requests that touched the group in the bucket.

fallbacks.description: Requests that needed more than one attempt.

latency_ms.description: Attempt latency percentiles (nearest rank); null without attempts.
